title: language-agnostic stream-transaction API and idempotent retry presets
author: Maya Rodriguez
description: This PR adds a language-agnostic 'stream transaction' abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and introduces a set of idempotent retry presets targeted at multi-message streaming operations. Motivation: production customers build streaming workflows that need composable, resumable sequences of messages (commit/abort semantics) and robust idempotent retries when transient infra errors happen mid-stream. Current SDK ergonomics make it awkward to express a logical transaction spanning multiple streamed messages; retry policies often either retry the whole session (unsafe) or leave callers to implement ad-hoc idempotency. This change provides: 1) a StreamTransaction API that lets callers open a transactional stream, emit messages, and either commit or abort; the SDKs translate this to underlying session+message semantics (lease-scoped sequence ids + at-least-once send with dedup keys). 2) IdempotentRetry presets (conservative, standard, aggressive) that encapsulate backoff/timeout/window behavior for streaming sends and reconnection; presets are tuned per-language to match platform idioms and integrate with existing session middlewares. 3) Ergonomic helpers: typed cursors for Python async iterators, a small TS pullstream facade aligned to existing async iterable patterns, and a Go StreamTxn builder with functional options. 4) Cross-sdk migration notes and version bumps: Python -> 2.8.0, TS -> 1.14.0, Go -> v1.7.0. 5) Compatibility shims: if callers do not opt-in, existing behavior remains unchanged. Implementation notes: - Added a lightweight transaction marker layer in the session transport to attach per-message sequence and dedup metadata; serverside forwarding was coordinated with platform team (ENG-1982) and a feature flag gate on the control plane. - Retry presets are implemented in each SDK's retry config module and wired through the stream send paths; they expose the same logical names so client code can be portable. - New unit/integration tests simulate mid-stream disconnects, duplicate message delivery, and mixed commit/abort outcomes. Checklist: [x] API design doc (linked in Linear) [x] Python/TS/Go implementations [x] Unit + integration tests [x] Migration notes and upgrade guide [x] Version bumps and changelogs [x] Feature-flagged server compatibility rollout Risks & mitigations: - Duplicate application-visible messages: mitigated by dedup keys tied to transaction IDs and monotonically increasing sequence numbers; server honors commit/abort window. - Long-running transactional streams holding resources: default transaction TTL is conservative (30s) and configurable; SDKs expose automatic keepalive heartbeats. - Complexity for simple streams: keep default autoresume/backoff behavior unchanged; StreamTransaction is opt-in only.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Introduce StreamTransaction abstraction + common interface across SDKs; 2) Implement per-language transports, retry presets, and tests; 3) Docs, changelogs, and version bumps.
review_comments: Samir Patel: Nice API surface — a few nits on naming. Suggest renaming Transaction.commit() -> finalize() to avoid collision with existing DB libs. Also please add an explicit 'transaction_id' visible in logs.

Maya Rodriguez: I prefer commit() as it's clearer to users; added transaction_id to the transport metadata and included a logging helper. Pushed patch to rename internal OpaqueTxn -> StreamTransaction but kept commit()/abort() on public API for ergonomics.
Elena Kim: Tests look good. Can we tighten the default TTL to 20s? Observability showed some long-tail leaks in canaries. Also add an opt-out for heartbeats.
Maya Rodriguez: Lowered default TTL to 25s after benchmarking; added StreamTransactionOptions.Keepalive(false) opt-out; updated docs and examples.
Jonah Li: CI flaky test 'TestStreamReattach' failed on first run; reran and it passed. Please add a flake ticket if it recurs.
Maya Rodriguez: Filed ENG-2015 to track the flake and added a short sleep/wait-backoff in the integration harness to reduce race surface.
Samir Patel: Approved after minor rename fix and changelog entries.
release_notes: Added StreamTransaction API to SDKs (Python 2.8.0, TS 1.14.0, Go v1.7.0). New idempotent retry presets (conservative/standard/aggressive) for streaming operations. StreamTransaction is opt-in and feature-flagged; see docs/guides/stream-transactions.md for migration steps and examples.
migration_notes: To opt-in: instantiate StreamTransaction via SDK factory (examples in examples/*). Existing streaming APIs unchanged. Upgrade advisable for workflows that need multi-message atomicity. Python: replace manual sequence keys with transaction.commit() flow; TS/Go similarly add commit/abort calls. Check server-side FF rollout before enabling in production.
notes_for_changelog: Cross-SDK: StreamTransaction (opt-in), idempotent retry presets, TTL and keepalive controls, SDK version bumps. See individual SDK CHANGELOG.md files for per-language details.
ci_details: Full CI: unit (pass), integration (pass after rerun of TestStreamReattach), lint (pass), docs-build (pass). One transient failure on first integration run; rerun succeeded.
qa_instructions: Run examples in examples/ with local feature flag enabled. Simulate mid-stream network drop and verify no duplicate final state when using commit() and that abort() leaves no side effects. Run integration tests with small TTL and ensure heartbeats can be toggled off.
maintainer_notes: Server-side gate must be enabled for tenant before clients enable StreamTransaction. Coordinate with platform release (ENG-1982) and support (SUP-4219) for staged rollout.
signoff: Maya Rodriguez (author) — Approved by Samir Patel, Elena Kim, Jonah Li
